persons.name: Black Partridge

present_on_scene_date.note: Presence on the afternoon of 14 August 1812, read from the evidence below; no source takes a roll call that afternoon.

persons.note: Chief; friendly to Kinzie and the garrison, but warned that the young men could not be restrained. Potawatomi, Illinois River (village opposite the head of Peoria Lake per Andreas; 'village on the Au Sable' per Wau-Bun). Helm (contemporary, 1814) puts him at Heald's quarters on the night of the 14th; Wau-Bun puts the medal return on the evening after the 14 Aug council. 15 and 16 August: per Wau-Bun (Mrs Helm's story) pulled Mrs Helm into the lake and led her to the camp; per Wau-Bun killed the wounded Lee girl; took Mrs Lee and infant to his village. 16th: sentinel on the Kinzie porch (Wau-Bun). Helm 1814 says only that his wife was among 'squaws' and does not mention the rescue. Afterwards: His village was later destroyed 'in a single day' (Andreas); ransomed Lt Helm from the Kankakee with pony, rifle and nose ring (Andreas, unsourced there).

evidence.locator: Appendix VI, Helm's narrative (1814), Gutenberg lines 16755-16757
evidence.quote: The night of the 14th the Interpreter and a Chief black patredge waited on Capt Heald the Indian gave up his medal
evidence.claim: Gave up his medal and warned Heald on the night of the 14th, with the interpreter
evidence.tier: contemporary (written 1812-1815 by a participant or from participants)

evidence.quote: Black Partridge, a Pottawatomie chief from the Illinois River, came to him with the significant message that "linden birds" had been singing in his ears
evidence.claim: Warning recorded as 'linden birds' (McAfee from Sgt Griffith); chief from the Illinois River
evidence.tier: secondary (Quaife) summarising two contemporary versions (Helm 1814; McAfee 1816 from Griffith)

evidence.quote: On the evening succeeding the council, _Black Partridge_, a conspicuous chief, entered the quarters of the commanding officer.
evidence.claim: Wau-Bun's medal speech, evening succeeding the second council of 14 Aug
evidence.tier: Kinzie family tradition (Wau-Bun; pamphlet 1836/1844, book 1856; Quaife App. II judges its speeches and dialogue invented)

evidence.quote: Mrs. Kinzie's version of his speech is just as certainly the product of her own literary imagination.
